title: qa(operator): track matching, application-truth and review findings for the next release
body:
## Operator findings for the next release

Recovered the available AI Job Hunter Operator message history and dated feedback from 12–16 October 2026, then cross-checked existing issues and the reviewed release source on 18 October. This is a follow-up to the device/sync audit, not another application campaign. No applications were submitted or real candidate records modified while filing these tickets.

The frozen 100-row historical sample had 81 footer-only descriptions, seven empty and 12 substantive/partial; all scored 100. Review passes overlap, so their dismissal totals must not be added into a unique-job claim. They establish screening defects, not interview conversion or a fully vetted pool.

## Fix order and ownership boundaries

1. Establish valid posting content, availability and identity before trusting ranking or starting preparation.
2. Make application/submission evidence and duplicate prevention truthful; preserve selected ad snapshots.
3. Ground fit/notes in versioned verified candidate evidence and explicit requirements.
4. Make the complete pool queryable and human review stable, reversible and understandable.
5. Reproduce uncertain parser and computer-control observations without assigning unsupported blame.

## Tracked work

- [ ] #1443 — fix(matching): reject footer-only descriptions before scoring and enrichment
- [ ] #1444 — feat(discovery): expose verified job availability separately from match score
- [ ] #1445 — fix(discovery): detect posting identity drift before replacing cached job content
- [ ] #1446 — fix(matching): ground fit explanations in verified candidate facts and mandatory requirements
- [ ] #1447 — fix(applications): distinguish preparation from submission evidence across duplicate checks
- [ ] #1448 — fix(agent): query and paginate the complete qualifying best-match set before the display cap
- [ ] #1449 — feat(review): add stable reversible match-review batches and explicit action side effects
- [ ] #1450 — fix(applications): preserve the selected job description when preparing a draft
- [ ] #1451 — investigate(import): reproduce resume name detection failure and preserve confirmed overrides

## Existing work and boundaries

#1433 portable preferences, #1434 sidebar/profile refresh, #1435/#1436 numeric sync precision, #1437 No-reply labels, #1438 photo disclosure, #1439 Documents Applied label, #1440 export content loss, #1442 bridge diagnostics remain separate and linked release work. #1441 fixes two UI badges, not the full submission-evidence model in this operator review.

Closed #1105/#1109 already added blank-content/provisional signals; #1114/#1117 added LinkedIn enrichment; #1104 exposed scoreUrl provenance; #1166 added canonical lookup; #1167 added compact cursor reads. New issues identify remaining gaps after those changes. #1179's lifecycle discussion is prior architecture context, not a reason to claim review batches or the full corpus UI are already validated.

The 16×16 maximized/multi-monitor input failure is tracked under the review compatibility note, not asserted as an application defect. Different UI/API first-page membership needs a controlled same-snapshot test; it is not proof that dismissal persistence failed. Parser-name extraction remains investigation pending a sanitized fixture.

## Release acceptance

Require regression fixtures for each confirmed P1 issue and a fresh installed-app pass on reachable Windows/macOS clients. Use disposable records for submission/migration/restore tests, preserve historical evidence, and verify sync preserves review decisions/overrides without copying device credentials. Missing text stays unknown, no invented candidate facts, no silent duplicate submissions, and no automatic destructive cleanup. Source checks alone do not certify every native workflow.

title: investigate(import): reproduce resume name detection failure and preserve confirmed overrides
body:
## Priority and evidence status
P2 investigation. Operator feedback on 12 October says importing a verified current résumé as default missed the candidate name and raised a review warning. The warning itself may be correct behavior for uncertain extraction; the underlying parser failure is not yet isolated with a sanitized synthetic fixture. Do not mark this confirmed against today's parser or upload the private résumé. The same review found a stale résumé employment date conflicting with confirmed profile facts, covered by the evidence-grounded matching follow-up.

## Proposed approach
Reproduce with private local evidence, then derive a minimal synthetic fixture preserving only the format that failed (Markdown/plain header, Unicode name, contact line order, relevant document type). If parsing is deficient, fix name extraction with confidence rather than guessing. Keep explicit review/edit and persist confirmed header overrides/default-document selection with provenance; never replace them with a later uncertain parse. Confirm which fields are portable under #1433 rather than adding credentials/transient UI state to sync.

## Acceptance tests
Synthetic supported header patterns yield the expected name, or explicit review-required state when ambiguous. Confirmed overrides survive reopen/restart/reimport and the supported sync path. Name/contact values seed Builder/generation consistently. No private source document, real identity/contact fields or fabricated candidate facts enter the public fixture.

Source: AI Job Hunter Operator review, 12–16 October 2026; source inspection on 18 October. Historical observations and source-confirmed mechanisms are distinguished above. No new application actions or candidate-data changes were performed to file this issue.

Related operator findings: #1446.

title: fix(applications): preserve the selected job description when preparing a draft
body:
## Priority and evidence
P1. On 12 October, drafts created through native Apply read back with empty stored jobDescription even though the source row/UI contained footer text; subsequently corrected live descriptions did not establish that earlier drafts were repaired. An empty snapshot and an invalid source are separate problems.

## Source-confirmed gap
`renderer/hooks/use-apply-to-found-job.ts` passes jobUrl/board/company/title/salary to saveFromPosting, but no jobDescription. The selected record may live in persisted autopilot storage rather than the ephemeral Jobs cache. Do not assume that a wizard display means the Application row contains the same text.

## Proposed fix
Resolve the exact selected posting's validated content through the canonical backend identity, or pass a bounded versioned source snapshot using the established AppClient/service contract. Persist description, quality and provenance atomically with draft creation, or expose explicit missing/needs-repair state. Reuse the quality gate from the content issue; never persist footer junk as verified text. Offer explicit refresh/diff for existing drafts after source repair, without overwriting user edits, generated materials or historical evidence.

## Acceptance tests
A substantive persisted-autopilot-only advert creates a Saved draft whose read-back content equals the selected validated source even when the Jobs cache is empty. A missing/boilerplate source creates a visibly incomplete draft, not a false complete one. Reopening/restarting/syncing preserves the snapshot and manual edits. Repairing a source does not silently replace an existing draft snapshot. No submission implied.

Source: AI Job Hunter Operator review, 12–16 October 2026; source inspection on 18 October. Historical observations and source-confirmed mechanisms are distinguished above. No new application actions or candidate-data changes were performed to file this issue.

Related operator findings: #1443, #1447.

title: feat(review): add stable reversible match-review batches and explicit action side effects
body:
## Priority and operator evidence
P2. Dismissals refilled a displayed 100-item list from a larger pool (357→305 in an initial pass), so a completed screen was not a completed review. One card moved during scroll animation and the wrong card was dismissed; Undo restored it. Apply created a Saved draft with appliedAt null, while the operator wanted only to open/review ads. Opening ads separately avoided ambiguous side effects.

## Proposed fix
Provide a stable frozen batch or snapshot cursor with total/reviewed/unreviewed counts, persisted reasons and reversible decisions/export. Separate Open advert, Save for review, Prepare application and explicit submission confirmation; explain which actions create records. Preserve existing working bookmark/Undo behavior rather than claim it is absent. Keep row actions bound to canonical job identity across async reorder/refill, provide an accessible named action target/keyboard confirmation, and avoid moving an active target while a dismissal interaction is resolving. No bulk dismissal merely for missing descriptions.

## Acceptance tests
A 100-visible/357-total pool cannot be labelled fully vetted after reviewing one page. Scroll/reorder plus delayed responses cannot silently apply a decision to another ID. Undo restores that exact job/reason across restart/sync. Open/copy/review creates no application. Preparing creates a clearly labelled draft and no submission evidence.

## Compatibility observation, not a proven app defect
On 16 October a maximized multi-monitor app screenshot was full-sized but the computer-use input target reported 16×16. Rebinding/activation did not recover it; input stopped before a pending Colgate dismissal. Track a controlled window/tool integration reproduction separately; inspect the main visible window vs helper HWND mapping, never blindly retry coordinates or classify the tool failure as an app dismissal bug.

Source: AI Job Hunter Operator review, 12–16 October 2026; source inspection on 18 October. Historical observations and source-confirmed mechanisms are distinguished above. No new application actions or candidate-data changes were performed to file this issue.

Related operator findings: #1448, #1447, #1444.

title: fix(agent): query and paginate the complete qualifying best-match set before the display cap
body:
## Priority and evidence
P2. Operator observed a job in found_jobs not reachable by Best Matches query; native UI showed 100 of 256 qualifying matches while connector total was capped at 100. A later UI first-page/native-vs-connector30 membership difference (flibco/TCL) is only a hypothesis until compared at the same snapshot/sort/filter. Do not call it dismissal-persistence failure.

## Source-confirmed mechanism
`commands/autopilot/best_matches.rs::compute_best_matches` computes total then truncates rows at BEST_MATCHES_CAP=100. `extension_bridge/agent_read/best_matches.rs::best_matches_resource` takes only raw.matches and passes that already-capped vector to resolve_best_matches, which applies query/paging and derives total. Cursor pagination from #1167 is present, but operates on the truncated subset; this is a follow-up, not a claim pagination never shipped.

## Proposed fix
Share a complete qualifying-query layer, apply query/filter/sort before paging, and make the native top-100 policy an explicit projection rather than the upstream search universe. Expose totalQualifying, totalFiltered, returned and nextCursor with consistent semantics and snapshot/query-bound cursors. Preserve compact byte budgets. Add a controlled same-snapshot UI/API parity test; explain legitimate cluster/sort/filter differences and exact/cluster membership rather than inferring lost dismissals.

## Acceptance tests
A unique matching title at rank 101+ can be searched and paginated. A 256-row fixture is fully traversable with accurate totals and no oversized responses. Dismiss/Undo and deterministic tie ordering preserve cursor semantics. UI and agent compare identical canonical IDs under identical predicates; default limit 30 is not presented as the entire pool.

Source: AI Job Hunter Operator review, 12–16 October 2026; source inspection on 18 October. Historical observations and source-confirmed mechanisms are distinguished above. No new application actions or candidate-data changes were performed to file this issue.

Related operator findings: #1447, #1449.

title: fix(applications): distinguish preparation from submission evidence across duplicate checks
body:
## Priority and operator evidence
P1. Best Matches still offered previously tracked/applied jobs. Exact job identity and an external read-only campaign ledger prevented duplicates (e.g. Morson 4474925440, Prysmian 4456724344, Italiaonline 4473626909). Starcom cluster 4464587887/4469679911/4401448648 reported applied=true while exact 4464587887 detail said false; scoreUrl pointed to another member. A Planetica record was withdrawn after an accidental manual track, yet retained appliedAt despite no actual submission.

## Source interpretation
`applications/writes.rs::upsert_for_origin` intentionally marks Generate/Manual/Backfill as applied; status history preserves first-applied timestamps. `best_matches.rs::mark_applied` ORs over cluster members. Thus some flag differences follow current semantics; do not label them proven data corruption. #1439/#1441 only remove an unsupported Documents badge; they do not solve this broader submission/duplicate contract. #1171 removed totalApplied from the agent projection, not submission ambiguity.

## Proposed fix
Model saved, preparing/started, submitted, withdrawn and interrupted-unknown with explicit provenance/evidence. Preparing/exporting documents or starting a wizard must not itself assert submission. Introduce an explicit confirmation/record-submission operation; preserve/version legacy manual-track behavior rather than silently breaking existing clients. Keep historical events but distinguish a legacy workflow timestamp from verified submittedAt.

Expose exact-posting and cluster-related status separately, including which member owns status and score. Before creating another application, canonical ID lookup should return/resume the existing draft or warn about submitted/unknown history. Provide an optional read-only external-ledger reconciliation/import adapter with source IDs and user review; do not rewrite an external campaign ledger or reinterpret an applied flag as a receipt. Company-wide waiting-period advice should be a separate warning, not an exact-requisition duplicate.

## Acceptance tests
Generate/prepare/export alone cannot create submission evidence. Same-ID regional URL variants and cluster copies have consistent exact-vs-related labels. Withdrawn legacy appliedAt never becomes a claimed receipt; interrupted state cannot silently retry submission. Existing drafts resume, known submissions warn/block duplicate creation, and an external-ledger mismatch stays explicit. Existing records are migrated conservatively with reversible review, no mass status rewrite.

Source: AI Job Hunter Operator review, 12–16 October 2026; source inspection on 18 October. Historical observations and source-confirmed mechanisms are distinguished above. No new application actions or candidate-data changes were performed to file this issue.

Related operator findings: #1450, #1448, #1449.

title: fix(matching): ground fit explanations in verified candidate facts and mandatory requirements
body:
## Priority and evidence
P1. Operator review found generic positive notes and saturated keyword scores overlooking hard requirements. Examples on 16 October: Prada 4478863536 required 7+ years CRM-related work and full professional Italian; Randstad Digital 4477059827 required 3–5 years commercial experience specifically consulting/IT. Earlier cases required specialist paid-ad platforms, sector tenure or fluent/C2 Italian. One note asserted fluent Italian despite the reviewed candidate evidence being A2–B1. These are historical observations, not new application decisions.

## Proposed fix
Represent must-have, preferred, transferable and unknown requirements separately, with evidence spans from the actual ad and the confirmed candidate profile. Produce fit category (supported fit / stretch / explicit gap / unknown), evidence confidence and authenticity/trust separately; keyword coverage 100 is not a 100% interview-fit probability. Version the candidate résumé/profile and job content used for score/notes. Invalidate stale notes when either changes. Treat an older résumé conflicting with confirmed facts as needs reconciliation. Preserve promising training-based stretches and missing-data cases for review; no fabricated skills, language, degree, licence, work eligibility or specialist years.

## Acceptance tests
A fixture candidate with A2–B1 Italian never gets a fluent-Italian claim. Generic commercial/CRM experience does not satisfy advanced paid-media platform tenure. Mandatory gaps are visible and affect fit, preferred gaps do not become absolute exclusions, and unknown eligibility stays unknown. A stale résumé cannot silently override a confirmed employment end date. Every positive factual assertion is traceable to the exact candidate/ad version; changed facts invalidate cached explanations. No auto-dismissal based only on title or missing data.

Source: AI Job Hunter Operator review, 12–16 October 2026; source inspection on 18 October. Historical observations and source-confirmed mechanisms are distinguished above. No new application actions or candidate-data changes were performed to file this issue.

Related operator findings: #1443, #1451, #1444.

title: fix(discovery): detect posting identity drift before replacing cached job content
body:
## Priority and evidence
P1 investigation from the 12 October operator review: a stored Clinora Milan BDR entry led to a closed UK Customer Success advert; a stored OMRON company was Aratas in the live ad. The exact cause (redirect, source metadata, stale cache or changed page) is not established. On 16 October a BYD Italy-titled ad explicitly required Spanish/English. A geographic/language inconsistency is not permission to silently rewrite its requirements.

## Proposed fix
Keep requested URL, resolved canonical posting identity, fetched-at/source and current extracted metadata distinct. Match board/requisition ID first; if job ID, employer, role or location materially changes, quarantine the refresh as identity-needs-review instead of silently attaching a different advert or carrying the old score/notes forward. Preserve raw evidence and user corrections. If the same legitimate posting has surprising requirements, retain its exact language and surface the inconsistency rather than changing it. Reuse canonical URL normalization from #1166; do not undo regional-host equivalence.

## Acceptance tests
Same-ID regional/slug redirects resolve correctly; a different requisition does not inherit the old candidate fit or submission status. Changed-company/role fixtures expose old/new metadata for review. Italy-title/Spanish-requirement fixture keeps Spanish explicit. No real records auto-deleted or silently reclassified.

Source: AI Job Hunter Operator review, 12–16 October 2026; source inspection on 18 October. Historical observations and source-confirmed mechanisms are distinguished above. No new application actions or candidate-data changes were performed to file this issue.

Related operator findings: #1443, #1447, #1444.

title: feat(discovery): expose verified job availability separately from match score
body:
## Priority and operator evidence
P1. High-scoring recommendations were live-checked closed/removed on 12 and 16 October 2026. Public posting IDs include Jet HR 4472247908/4472255738, Grafton 4465215207/4459511367, Aegis 4464992414, Lenovo 4428081330, Antal 4465069579 and Colgate 4454770323. These observations describe those review dates; no claim is made that all pages were re-fetched today.

## Proposed fix
Persist availability as open, closed, removed or unknown, with checkedAt, source and a sanitized evidence category. Add a bounded, rate-limited verification queue for recommendations and explicit on-demand refresh. Separate cached discovery from currently verified actionable recommendations. Treat 403/login/captcha/timeouts and generic fetch failures as unknown, never closed. Use recoverable archive/dismissal with clear reason and Undo; preserve historical records and distinguish reposted requisition IDs.

## Acceptance tests
Captured closed/removed fixtures do not appear as actionable open recommendations. Unknown network/auth failures remain visible for review with stale/unknown labels. Reopening and reposting do not inherit another requisition's closure. Refreshes survive navigation/restart and expose the same state/timestamp to UI and agent readers. No uncontrolled background crawling or automatic deletion.

Source: AI Job Hunter Operator review, 12–16 October 2026; source inspection on 18 October. Historical observations and source-confirmed mechanisms are distinguished above. No new application actions or candidate-data changes were performed to file this issue.

Related operator findings: #1443, #1445, #1449.

title: fix(matching): reject footer-only descriptions before scoring and enrichment
body:
## Priority and evidence
P1. Operator review on 12 October 2026 captured a frozen 100-record Best Matches snapshot: all scored 100, 81 descriptions were LinkedIn footer text, seven empty, 12 substantive or partial. These are historical snapshot counts, not a fresh measurement of today's pool.

## Existing fixes and remaining mechanism
#1105/#1109 already added blank-content/provisional signals; #1114/#1117 already added bounded LinkedIn enrichment. Do not claim enrichment is absent. In the reviewed release source, `documents/keywords/posting.rs::description_is_blank` only tests whether stripped text is empty; meaningful-looking footer/login/navigation text survives. `autopilot_helpers/linkedin_enrich.rs` selects blank descriptions, so a nonempty bad enrichment can cease being eligible. Existing generic HTML quality extraction does not prove stored historical rows were repaired.

## Proposed fix
Share an explicit content-quality classifier across ingest, enrichment, scoring and UI/API projection: missing, boilerplate, partial, substantive. Preserve original text and source, expose needs-description-review independently from fit/trust, and permit manual paste/refresh without Apply. Re-enrich invalid nonempty content with bounded retry/rate limits. Version text and invalidate dependent score/AI-note caches when the content changes; offer a bounded preview/backfill for historical contaminated rows. Do not auto-dismiss jobs solely for missing descriptions.

## Acceptance tests
- Empty, URL-only, login-wall, footer-only and mixed-footer fixtures never yield an unqualified high-fit claim.
- A short genuine ad is not rejected solely by length; multilingual substantive fixtures remain usable.
- Failed fetch remains unknown; manual paste updates score provenance and survives resurfacing/sync.
- Existing valid text and user corrections are not overwritten by lower-quality enrichment.

Source: AI Job Hunter Operator review, 12–16 October 2026; source inspection on 18 October. Historical observations and source-confirmed mechanisms are distinguished above. No new application actions or candidate-data changes were performed to file this issue.

Related operator findings: #1444, #1445, #1446, #1450.

title: fix(bridge): distinguish occupied discovery ports from app not running
body:
## Installed-app failure and bounded diagnosis

On one Windows host running v0.158.0, the visible desktop app runs normally but its agent CLI reports unavailable. The bridge cannot bind any port in its fixed six-port discovery range. Standalone IPv4 and IPv6 loopback bind probes fail on those ports with Windows error 10048; binding loopback port 0 succeeds. Windows connection inventory shows no listener for the fixed range, and the displayed excluded ranges do not overlap it. The underlying OS/network cause remains unknown.

`extension_bridge/server.rs::probe_ports` discards bind errors and disables the bridge when the entire range fails. A user cannot distinguish a stopped app from an app whose local bridge failed to initialize.

Please expose a sanitized bind failure diagnostic in the app/CLI, and document or implement a safe recovery strategy consistent with extension discovery. Do not silently expand discovery or reset users' networking. Regression coverage should occupy every configured port and verify the resulting diagnostic/recovery state. This issue records a reproducible symptom and an observability gap, not a proven root cause in the application.

title: fix(export): preserve education and dates beneath Markdown entry headings
body:
## Reproduction on installed v0.158.0

Export this synthetic résumé through `commands:documents_export_document`, documentType `resume`, locale `en`, template `classic`, once as PDF and once as DOCX:

```markdown
Jane Doe
jane@example.test | Turin, Italy

## Experience
### Business Analyst | Example Company
January 2022 - Present
- Prepared weekly market reports and coordinated project schedules.

## Education
### Bachelor of Business Administration | Example University
2018 - 2021

## Skills
Market research, project coordination, spreadsheet analysis.
```

The produced DOCX text omits Education, the degree/university and dates. The experience date is also absent. Export returns `ok: true` with missing-section warnings. All 16 résumé templates in PDF and DOCX reproduced missing-education warnings (32 structurally valid files); this is not a clean content-preservation pass.

Control: remove only the two `### ` prefixes. Classic PDF/DOCX then return no validation issues and preserve the education content. This isolates heading interpretation rather than AI output, provider credentials or a corrupt file. No real candidate records were edited.

Please preserve nested entry headings and their date-only content, and add content-level regressions for both outputs. Structural validity alone must not certify résumé correctness. Root-cause investigation should distinguish parser classification from adapter empty-section dropping.

title: fix(privacy): photo hint contradicts opt-in self-hosted sync
body:
## Reproduction (v0.158.0)

Open Resume Builder's contact-details step with a saved photo. Its photo hint says:

> Kept on your device only — never uploaded.

With optional self-hosted sync enabled, `contactProfile` includes that photo, so it is intentionally uploaded to the configured user-owned sync server and received by another device. The photo synced correctly between two real Windows installations, but this local-only promise is no longer accurate.

## Source / scope

- `resumeBuilder.photoHint` in the English translation file.
- Contact-profile export and its single-object sync section.
- The corresponding German copy should also be reviewed.

This is a disclosure defect, not a request to remove photo synchronization. It does not indicate a photo was sent to the app operator or an AI provider.

## Expected

Describe where the photo is used and distinguish local rendering from explicitly enabled backup/sync. Review similar local-only promises against the opt-in sync egress exception introduced in #1402. Add a regression that prevents this unconditional device-only promise from returning.

No private photo, contact details, server address or credentials are included in this report.

title: fix(sync): preserve numeric payloads across json round trips
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1435. JSON parsing can change an unchanged floating-point usage cost by one rounding step, so two synced installations export different payloads and hashes for the same usage record. Enable serde_json's `float_roundtrip` feature to preserve the original numeric payload through the wire round trip.

## Type of change

- [x] `fix` — Bug fix

## Changes

- Enable the existing dependency's round-trip float parser; no version bump, new crate, server change or protocol change.
- Regress three non-zero cost values at payload/value and hash level.
- Seed a non-zero high-precision cost in the all-store fixture, so its existing two-client HTTP convergence test exercises this case instead of zero only.

## Testing

- [x] Full Rust library suite: **6,065 passed, 27 ignored, zero failed**.
- [x] Sync subset: **44 passed**, including real-store two-client HTTP convergence and the new numeric hash regression.
- [x] `cargo fmt --check`, `git diff --check`.
- A standalone diagnostic using the exact lockfile serde_json version changed `0.00009500900000000001` into `0.000095009` with the old default parser. The new feature preserved all three test values exactly.
- Two installed v0.158.0 Windows snapshots contained 202 shared usage rows differing only by tiny cost rounding. The standalone reproduction isolates the parsing issue; it does not claim materially incorrect bills or lost application data.

The patched native apps have not been installed on the production devices. A fresh real Windows ⇄ server ⇄ macOS test remains outstanding because the Mac is currently unreachable. This is therefore a draft for review, not a claim of full-device validation.

## Checklist

The branch also includes the minimal README/SECURITY wording correction required by `check:landing-drift`; the local disclosure check passes. The earlier hosted lint failure was this disclosure gate, not the precision regression. Hosted checks on the new head must pass separately.

- [x] Conventional commit
- [x] Tests added; no suppressions
- [x] No credentials, personal data or deployment addresses
- [x] No new public API

Existing rounded historical values are not reconstructed automatically by this change.

title: fix(sync): preserve floating-point payloads across the json wire round trip
body:
## Observed behavior

Two Windows v0.158.0 clients using the same self-hosted namespace hold matching usage-record IDs but different exact cost values and record hashes. A snapshot comparison found 202 shared `ai_spend` rows differing only in `est_cost_usd`, by one floating-point rounding step. New usage rows waiting for a pull were counted separately.

## Reproduction

With the lockfile's serde_json version and its current default features:

```rust
let payload = serde_json::json!({"estCostUsd": 9.500900000000001e-05_f64});
let wire = serde_json::to_string(&payload).unwrap();
let received: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&wire).unwrap();
assert_eq!(payload, received); // fails
```

The wire value `0.00009500900000000001` parses back as `0.000095009`. Enabling serde_json's `float_roundtrip` feature preserves the original value in this reproduction.

## Expected behavior

Unchanged numeric payloads survive the JSON wire round trip exactly, so the same usage record exports and hashes identically on both devices. This is a precision/convergence problem, not evidence of materially incorrect billing totals or lost application records.

Related to #1402. I am preparing a minimal dependency-feature fix and regression coverage, including the real-store two-client HTTP fixture with a non-zero cost. No server or protocol change is proposed.

title: fix(sync): show received profiles and refresh open screens
body:
## Summary

A fresh synced installation can contain a contact profile and photo but hide the sidebar identity because its local display nickname is empty. A short window can also clip the identity footer and Settings link. Manual sync updates only the status cache, while background sync has no renderer refresh path, leaving already-open screens stale.

Use the synced contact name as a fallback for the sidebar/dashboard, and mount a root-level local sync-status observer that invalidates affected store queries when a successful run applied records. Existing explicit nicknames are preserved. Add English/German copy explaining the settings excluded from sync and its startup/periodic/manual cadence.

Part of #1433; related to #1402. **This does not extend the sync payload to renderer preferences.** That scope extension remains the design question in #1433.

## Type of change

- [x] `fix` — Bug fix

## Changes

- Contact-profile fallback without writing a local nickname or overwriting an explicit one.
- Scroll the main navigation while keeping the footer and Settings visible in short windows.
- App-global refresh after manual/configure/background status changes; no new network sync or IPC capability. Background UI refresh follows the existing local status polling interval.
- Only store-backed queries are invalidated; credentials, AI probes/model lists and the sync-status query are excluded.
- Clear coverage disclosure for display nicknames, appearance, language and other renderer settings.
- Name self-hosted sync explicitly in the README/security disclosure to match the egress inventory, and replace the vague word “settings” with the actual backend setting categories. The landing-drift check previously failed on this same missing name on main.

## Testing

- [x] Six additional navigation tests passed: all 12 workspace routes and all 12 settings sections in English/German at 900×540, 1280×720 and 1440×900. Settings selection and visible section descriptions are asserted. These use the mock client; its undefined system-metric warnings remain a fixture limitation, not proof of native health.
- Photo help text now discloses app backups and enabled self-hosted sync in both languages, instead of promising the synced photo is never uploaded. Fixes #1438.

- [x] Full desktop renderer suite: 4,451 passed (423 files).
- [x] Desktop TypeScript check and frontend production build.
- [x] ESLint with zero warnings on changed renderer files, Prettier, whitespace, event-subscription and TS size checks.
- [x] Regression tests cover the received contact-name fallback, explicit nickname, missing profile, cache refresh on received data, repeated status/no-op runs and excluded credential queries.
- [x] Nine Playwright browser tests passed. Sidebar cases at 540/640/720/900 px explicitly check Help & Support, Settings, profile and version, scroll navigation to Monitoring, and open Settings. Original sidebar negative control: fails at 540/640/720 px, passes at 900 px. Patched sidebar: passes all four. This uses the mock-client renderer, not a patched native device.
- Installed v0.158.0 on two real Windows devices: contact-profile snapshots match, including the photo, while the display name differed. The receiving device's display name was repaired separately through Settings. Those observations reproduce the issue; they are **not** a claim that these patched binaries ran on both devices.
- The actual Mac is unreachable in this test session. A new Windows ⇄ server ⇄ macOS native-app test is still outstanding.

## Checklist

- [x] Conventional commit
- [x] No debug logs or type/lint suppressions
- [x] No credentials, personal records or deployment addresses included
- [x] No new public API

No installed production executable has been replaced by this branch. Please review alongside the scope question in #1433 before release.

  * Improved sidebar navigation scrolling and kept footer links and account details visible on shorter screens.

title: feat(sync): include portable profile and preferences in the shared workspace
body:
## Problem

After enabling v0.158.0 self-hosted sync on two Windows installations, the receiving installation has the same contact-profile database (including its photo), applications and documents, but still looks like a different profile. The sidebar hides the entire profile block unless renderer-local `userName` is set. The dashboard also reads that local name. This is reproducible even after reopening the receiving app.

This follows #1402 and merged #1418, #1427, #1430 and #1431. The agreed v1 scope was the export bundle. The engine follows that boundary, but users who expect to continue the same workspace on another device also need portable preferences that are outside that bundle.

## Verified gaps

- `renderer/store/preferences-store/preferences-store.ts` persists `userName`, language, output tone, résumé-processing options, applicant facts, prompt quality and provider tuning in webview localStorage (`ai-job-hunter-preferences`). They are absent from `commands/data.rs::build_bundle` and `sync_scheduler::with_sections`. The actual default-document flag already syncs through `documents.isDefault`; a legacy renderer default-id field must not be mistaken for the active default selector.
- `packages/ui/src/lib/theme.ts` separately persists appearance as `ajh-theme`.
- The sidebar's photo is in `contactProfile`, but the whole block is gated by the unsynced display name.
- `useSyncNow` and `useConfigureSync` update only the sync-status query. The scheduler applies store changes without notifying renderer queries. Already-open screens can keep displaying pre-sync data.
- Background sync runs after startup and periodically, not on each user edit. It is not instant workspace mirroring.

## Requested outcome

Let a user move between devices with the same portable profile and preferences, using the existing private server, while preserving local-first and offline operation.

Before expanding the wire payload, please confirm the scope, as requested in #1402:

1. Include portable preferences in backup and per-record sync: display name, language, output tone, résumé-processing choices, applicant start/notice/remote facts, prompt quality/reasoning settings, recent locations, and user-selected appearance. Reconcile existing backend mirrors such as salary without replacing their established ownership. The actual default résumé is already carried by document records.
2. Define which hardware/window settings remain per-device (performance, local model limits/paths, launch-at-login, close-to-tray), and which require explicit per-device consent (logo enrichment, indexing, extension permissions, email watching). Do not silently transport API keys, pairing secrets, auth sessions or keychain entries.
3. Use a backend-owned, versioned, allowlisted preferences store with a safe one-time migration from existing renderer storage. Avoid stale renderer mirrors overwriting received changes on launch.
4. Define per-preference conflict/reset semantics and old-client behavior. New sections must be held by older clients without breaking their existing sections.
5. Refresh open screens after manual and background sync, and disclose the actual coverage and interval in Settings.

## Acceptance evidence needed

- Fresh receiving install displays the contact name/photo and selects the synced default résumé.
- Portable preference edits travel both directions and survive app reopen; default settings on a fresh device do not overwrite existing settings.
- Offline edits, conflicts, interrupted runs, retries and schema-version holds remain safe.
- No secrets, machine-local paths, permissions or caches are introduced into the sync payload inadvertently.
- Renderer queries refresh after a received change while the page stays open.
- Real Windows ⇄ self-hosted server ⇄ macOS evidence; fixture tests are labeled separately.

Two live Windows installations were inspected and their SQLite snapshots passed integrity checks. The actual macOS host is currently unreachable, so this report does not claim a new live Mac test. No personal data, server addresses or credentials are included here.

I am preparing a small fix for profile visibility, renderer refresh and coverage disclosure separately. That does not claim to implement this broader portable-preferences extension.

title: feat: optional self-hosted multi-device sync that keeps local-first storage
body:
## Problem

AI Job Hunter is local-first: applications, autopilots, found jobs, documents, generations and settings live in SQLite/JSON stores on one machine, with no app-operated backend. That is the right default for privacy.

The cost shows up as soon as someone uses two computers (for example a Windows desktop at home and a MacBook on the move). Today the only way to move state between them is **Settings → Privacy → export / import**, and import is deliberately a full **REPLACE** (`DataStore::import`, `commands/data.rs`). So:

- moving state is manual and has to be repeated every time you switch machines;
- if both machines were used since the last export, importing on one silently discards whatever the other did (a new application, a status change, a note, a follow-up date);
- there is no way to keep a "current" view on both devices.

## Proposed solution

**Optional, self-hosted sync — bring your own sync server.** Local-first stays the default and nothing changes for anyone who doesn't turn it on.

```
Windows (local SQLite, authoritative copy)
        ⇅  HTTPS, opaque change batches
user-owned sync endpoint  (home server, NAS, Raspberry Pi, VPS, Docker host)
        ⇅
macOS (local SQLite, authoritative copy)
```

- The project never hosts user data. The user supplies a server URL and a sync token.
- Every device stays fully usable offline; sync is a background reconcile, never a dependency.
- Secrets never sync: OS-keychain contents (provider API keys, the email-watch app password) stay device-local.

### What I found in the current source (main @ 590013a, v0.157.0)

- `docs/DESIGN_DECISIONS.md` already names the `DataStore` export bundle as "the foundation any future sync feature would build on". The bundle has 13 sections: `documents`, `aiGenerations`, `applications`, `referrals`, `autopilots` (incl. found jobs since #1281), `interactions`, `spend`, `dedupTombstones`, `discoveredCompanies`, `jobPreferences`, `contactProfile`, `aiProviderConfig`, `pipelineRuns`.
- Excluded by design and should stay device-local: keychain credentials, `email_watch.db` (machine-local UID watermark), caches, `jobs.db`, `board_health.db`, notifications, vectors/embeddings (regenerable).
- The bundle is a whole-snapshot format with REPLACE import. That is correct for backup/restore but **not** safe as a sync primitive: copying a snapshot (or a live SQLite file) between two devices that both changed loses data.
- Record identity already exists (import "preserves record ids"), and some stores carry `updated_at` (e.g. `applications`), but there is no uniform per-record revision/deletion marker across stores yet. That gap is the real core of this feature.
- ADR 0005 (network egress privacy boundary) would need an amendment: a user-configured sync endpoint is a new egress, similar in spirit to the opt-in IMAP watcher.

### Suggested direction (open for discussion — not decided)

1. **Record-level change log on top of `DataStore`, not database replication.** Each synced store exposes "changes since revision N" and "apply remote changes". A change is a small envelope:
   `{ store, recordId, rev (hybrid logical clock), deviceId, deleted, schemaVersion, payload }`.
2. **A deliberately dumb server.** Authenticated (bearer sync token) append-only log per namespace: `POST /changes`, `GET /changes?since=<cursor>`, `GET /health` (with protocol version). It never needs to understand the payload, which makes **end-to-end encryption cheap to add** (encrypt `payload` client-side with a key derived from a user passphrase) — could be v1 or a fast follow.
3. **Deterministic conflicts per entity type:**
   - records (applications, autopilots, preferences, profile): last-writer-wins on the HLC revision, ties broken by deviceId;
   - append-only data (status events, spend rows, pipeline events): union, never overwrite;
   - documents: content-addressed immutable blobs + metadata record;
   - deletions: tombstones, so a delete on one device can't be resurrected by another.
4. **Schema compatibility:** every envelope carries its store schema version; a client stores but does not apply changes from a newer schema until it is updated, and never down-converts.
5. **Failure safety:** sync never overwrites the local store wholesale. Apply happens per record inside the store's own transaction; an interrupted upload/download just resumes from the last acknowledged cursor; a malformed server response is rejected, not applied.

### Possible incremental plan (to keep each PR reviewable)

1. ADR + protocol doc (envelope, endpoints, conflict rules, egress amendment). No runtime change.
2. Change capture for 2–3 stores first (`applications` incl. status events, `contactProfile`, `jobPreferences`) behind a disabled-by-default flag, with in-memory-SQLite tests for merge/conflict/tombstone cases.
3. Minimal reference server (single binary or tiny container, SQLite-backed) + a contract test suite any third-party server can run.
4. Client sync engine + **Settings → Data → Sync** card (enable, server URL, token, device name, test connection, sync now, last sync, health).
5. Remaining stores and documents/blobs.

## Acceptance criteria (for the eventual feature)

- [ ] With sync disabled, behaviour and on-disk data are unchanged.
- [ ] Two devices pointed at the same server converge: a change made on A appears on B after a sync, and vice versa.
- [ ] Editing on both devices while offline, then syncing, yields the same deterministic result on both, with no silent loss of append-only history (status events).
- [ ] Deleting a record on one device deletes it on the other and it does not reappear.
- [ ] The app remains fully usable with the server unreachable; sync resumes automatically.
- [ ] No keychain secret, app password or API key is ever sent to the server.
- [ ] Interrupting a sync (kill the app mid-upload/download) never corrupts or wipes the local store.
- [ ] A client on an older schema does not misapply changes from a newer one.
- [ ] Works on Windows and macOS (no platform paths in the protocol); the server runs anywhere (Linux/Docker/Pi/NAS).
- [ ] The sync token is never logged and never appears in crash reports.

## Alternatives considered

- **Sync the export bundle (whole snapshot) through a server/folder.** Smallest to build, but REPLACE semantics loses data whenever both devices changed — not acceptable as sync.
- **Sync the SQLite files (Dropbox/OneDrive/Syncthing).** Unsafe with WAL-mode databases and concurrent writers; also covers secrets-adjacent and machine-local files.
- **SQLite replication / CRDT frameworks (cr-sqlite, Automerge, ElectricSQL, etc.).** Powerful, but they would touch every store's schema and add a large dependency for a problem a per-record LWW + tombstone log already solves for this data model.
- **A hosted AI Job Hunter cloud.** Contradicts the local-first / no-backend principle and puts user data on the maintainer.

## Additional context

I'm a daily user on Windows who also works from a Mac, and I'd like to help implement this. Before writing code I'd value your view on:

1. Is optional self-hosted sync welcome in the project at all?
2. Is a record-level change log on top of `DataStore` the direction you'd accept, or would you prefer a different foundation?
3. Should the reference server live in this monorepo (e.g. `apps/sync-server`) or in a separate repository?
4. Is the first PR you'd want the ADR/protocol, or a small change-capture slice for `applications` only?

I can run a real two-device test (Windows ⇄ self-hosted server ⇄ macOS) for every slice.
